newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. June T-bonds quietly trade higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. June T-bonds quietly trade higher.

text.p: U.S. June T-bond futures quietly traded higher, but the results of Thursday's five-year note auction could shake the contract from its inside-day range, technical analysts said.
September T-bonds become lead contract month at the start of Thursday's evening session.

June T-bonds tested the daily high of 109-04/32 at midday. However, they are expected to make a final foray as lead contract month to the support area of 108-20/32 to 108-17/32 if the U.S. Treasury Department's auction is greeted with weak demand, they said.
One futures trader said longs would aggressively liquidate positions if June broke to 108-16/32, below the four-week low of 108-17/32.
The 108-17/32 level also represents a 50 percent retracement of June's rally off the 8-1/2-month low of 106-12/32.

Bruce Kamich, senior vice president at MCM MoneyWatch said June T-bonds' decline to 106-12/32 on April 11 may have signaled a long-term bottom. That level was nearly 10 points below the 1-1/4-year high of 116-00 reached on December 3.
"By observation we have found that 10 points is a typical major move for bonds," Kamich said. "After these 10-point runs, bonds often consolidate or reverse."

Kamich also noted that a 40-week cycle bottomed in mid-April, indicating that T-bonds could trade higher until late August or early September. That cycle projection coincides with a weekly trend change anticipated by Kamich for early September. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
